# dlamrg

> Creates a permutation list to merge the entries of two independently sorted sets into a single set sorted in ascending order.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlamrg from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlamrg';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlamrg( n1, n2, a, strideA, dtrd1, dtrd2, INDEX, strideINDEX ) → Int32Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `n1` | `NonNegativeInteger` | These arguments contain the respective lengths of the two sorted lists to be merged. |
| `n2` | `NonNegativeInteger` | These arguments contain the respective lengths of the two sorted lists to be merged. |
| `a` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length n1 + n2</sub> | The first N1 elements of A contain a list of numbers which are sorted in either ascending or descending order. |
| ↳ `strideA` | `integer` | Stride length for `a` |
| `dtrd1` | `integer` | These are the strides to be taken through the array A. |
| `dtrd2` | `integer` | These are the strides to be taken through the array A. |
| `INDEX` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length n1 + n2</sub> | **out** · On exit this array will contain a permutation such that if B( I ) = A( INDEX( I ) ) for I=1,N1+N2, then B will be sorted in ascending order (0-based). |
| ↳ `strideINDEX` | `integer` | Stride length for `INDEX` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `n2`: These arguments contain the respective lengths of the two sorted lists to be merged.
- `a`: The first `N1` elements of A contain a list of numbers which are sorted in either ascending or descending order. Likewise for the final `N2` elements.
- `dtrd2`: These are the strides to be taken through the array A. Allowable strides are 1 and -1. They indicate whether a subset of A is sorted in ascending (DTRDx = 1) or descending (DTRDx = -1) order.
- `INDEX`: On exit this array will contain a permutation such that if $B( I ) = A( \mathrm{INDEX}( I ) )$ for $I=1$,`N1`+`N2`, then B will be sorted in ascending order.

</details>

**Returns** `Int32Array`: `INDEX`

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlamrg.ndarray(
    n1, n2,
    a, strideA, offsetA,
    dtrd1, dtrd2,
    INDEX, strideINDEX, offsetINDEX
) → Int32Array
```

Merges two sorted integer sublists into a single sorted list.

Given two sorted sublists (from the array A), this routine creates
a single sorted list in INDEX. The sublists are A(0:N1-1) and
A(N1:N1+N2-1) in 0-based indexing (Fortran: A(1:N1) and A(N1+1:N1+N2)).

The parameter DTRD1/DTRD2 controls whether each sublist is traversed
forward (+1) or backward (-1).

NOTE: INDEX values are 1-based (Fortran convention) as they are used
internally by the divide-and-conquer eigensolver.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `n1` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Length of first sorted sublist |
| `n2` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Length of second sorted sublist |
| `a` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length n1 + n2</sub> | Array containing two sorted sublists |
| ↳ `strideA` | `integer` | Stride for a |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for a |
| `dtrd1` | `integer` | Direction for first sublist (+1 forward, -1 backward) |
| `dtrd2` | `integer` | Direction for second sublist (+1 forward, -1 backward) |
| `INDEX` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length n1 + n2</sub> | **out** · Output merged index list (1-based values) |
| ↳ `strideINDEX` | `integer` | Stride for INDEX |
| ↳ `offsetINDEX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for INDEX |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `n2`: These arguments contain the respective lengths of the two sorted lists to be merged.
- `a`: The first `N1` elements of A contain a list of numbers which are sorted in either ascending or descending order. Likewise for the final `N2` elements.
- `dtrd2`: These are the strides to be taken through the array A. Allowable strides are 1 and -1. They indicate whether a subset of A is sorted in ascending (DTRDx = 1) or descending (DTRDx = -1) order.
- `INDEX`: On exit this array will contain a permutation such that if $B( I ) = A( \mathrm{INDEX}( I ) )$ for $I=1$,`N1`+`N2`, then B will be sorted in ascending order.

</details>

**Returns** `Int32Array`: `INDEX`

</section>

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlamrg()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLAMRG`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlamrg.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import dlamrg from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlamrg';

// Two sorted sublists: [ 1, 3, 5 ] (ascending) and [ 6, 4, 2 ] (descending):
const a = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 3.0, 5.0, 6.0, 4.0, 2.0 ] );
const INDEX = new Int32Array( 6 );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = dlamrg( 3, 3, a, 1, 1, -1, INDEX, 1 );
console.log( out );

// Using the ndarray interface:
out = dlamrg.ndarray( 3, 3, a, 1, 0, 1, -1, INDEX, 1, 0 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>
